did_you_know.text: Did you know? According to the verse, King Ahasuerus ruled over 127 provinces, from India to Cush.
Did you know? Susa is described as “Susa the citadel”—the center of government where the king sat on his royal throne.
Did you know? In the third year of his reign, Ahasuerus held a feast for his officials and servants, attended by the army of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the provincial officials.
Did you know? The feast for the kingdom’s officials lasted 180 days, during which the king displayed the wealth and splendor of his glorious kingdom.
Did you know? After the lengthy feast, the king held another feast for all the people in Susa the citadel, lasting seven days, from the greatest to the least.
Did you know? The feast’s drinking was described as “according to the law, without compulsion”—meaning that everyone could drink as much as they wished, without being forced.
Did you know? At the same time as the king’s feast, Queen Vashti held a separate feast for the women in the royal palace of King Ahasuerus.
Did you know? On the seventh day, when the king was cheerful from the wine, he sent seven eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti before him.
Did you know? Vashti refused to come at the king’s command. As a result, Ahasuerus became very angry, and his fury burned within him.

Did you know? The decree sent throughout the kingdom was written for each province in its own script and for each people in its own language. It declared that every man should be master of his own household and speak the language of his people.
